issues.legal_issue: A tenancy created by a mortgagee in possession does not bind the owners after redemption when it was not prudent management and the owners did not adopt the tenancy.
material_facts: The mortgagee in possession let the premises to the appellant during the mortgage.
The District Judge found that the lease was not an act of prudent management.
The rent agreement required the appellant to vacate and hand over the premises if the owner obtained their release from the mortgage.
After redemption, the owners sought possession, and there was no agreement by them to continue the tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy created by the mortgagee did not survive redemption and did not bind the owners; the appellant could not resist their claim for possession on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 76(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, acts done bona fide and prudently in the ordinary course of management may bind the owner after the mortgage ends, though that principle has seldom been extended to urban property. A tenancy created by a mortgagee in possession ends with the mortgagee’s interest unless the mortgagor or successor agrees to it or creates a fresh tenancy. The Court relied on All India Film Corporation Ltd. v. Sri Rajgyan Nath, Mahabir Gope v. Harbansnarain Singh, and Asaram v. Mst. Ram Kali.

rule.if: redemption_dispute and mortgagee_created_lease and lease_not_prudent and owners_did_not_adopt_tenancy

predicates.redemption_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to possession after a mortgage has been redeemed.
predicates.mortgagee_created_lease: A mortgagee in possession let the property to a tenant during the mortgage.
predicates.lease_not_prudent: The lease was found not to be a prudent act in the ordinary course of managing the property.
predicates.owners_did_not_adopt_tenancy: The owners neither agreed to continue the tenancy nor created a fresh tenancy after redemption.

issues.definition: When a mortgagee creates a lease that is not prudent and the owners do not adopt it, the lease does not bind them after redemption.

issues.legal_issue: Rent-control protection does not continue for a tenant whose tenancy created by a mortgagee in possession ends upon redemption, absent a continuing or newly created tenancy with the owners.
material_facts: The appellant claimed protection under the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, against eviction without proceedings under that Act.
The tenancy had been created by the mortgagee in possession and did not survive redemption.
The owners did not agree to continue the tenancy or create a fresh tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The appellant could not rely on the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act to prevent the owners from obtaining possession because, after redemption, no landlord-and-tenant relationship remained between them and the appellant.
issues.legal_principle: The landlord and tenant definitions in the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act are similar to those considered in All India Film Corporation Ltd. v. Sri Rajgyan Nath. Those definitions presuppose a tenancy, real or statutory, that survives the mortgagee’s interest; when that interest ends and no tenancy continues or is recreated, the Act does not apply. The Court also referred to Kamalakar & Co. v. Gulatnsha.fi Jmambhai Mussalman and Bhanshali Khushalchand Shamji v. Shah Shamji Jivraj.

predicates.rent_control_claim_after_mortgage_redemp: The tenant claims statutory rent-control protection against possession being recovered after mortgage redemption.
predicates.mortgagee_tenancy_ended: The tenancy created by the mortgagee ended when the mortgagee’s interest ended.
predicates.owners_did_not_create_new_tenancy: The owners did not agree to continue the tenancy or create a new tenancy.

issues.definition: If a tenant claims rent-control protection after redemption but the mortgagee-created tenancy has ended and the owners have not created a new tenancy, that protection is unavailable.
